subject: english-literature
title: Propp's Functions
welcome_lead: Vladimir Propp dissected a hundred Russian folk tales and found thirty-one functions. Trace his anatomy.
meta_desc: Propp's morphology of the folktale and character functions at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have walked through Propp's syntax of story — and seen how Hollywood still uses his grammar.

concepts.def: Vladimir Propp (1928) analysed 100 Russian folktales and identified 31 recurring narrative functions in a fixed order.
Propp's units of action — absentation, prohibition, violation, villainy, struggle, victory, return etc.
Propp identified seven character spheres: hero, villain, helper, donor, princess, dispatcher, false hero.
Propp influenced Lévi-Strauss, Barthes and modern screenwriting templates.
Joseph Campbell (1949) extracted a mythic monomyth pattern overlapping with Propp's functions.
A. J. Greimas refined Propp into six actantial roles arranged in three oppositional pairs.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Propp argued that beneath the surface variety of folktales lay a single grammar — 31 functions in a fixed order.

Not every tale uses all 31, but those that appear maintain the sequence.

Each tale features roles: hero, villain, helper (a wise animal), donor (gives magic object), princess (the prize), dispatcher (sends hero off), false hero (claims credit).

One character can occupy multiple roles; one role can be filled by multiple characters.

walkthroughs.h2: The Hero with a Thousand Faces
walkthroughs.body_html: Joseph Campbell's monomyth (1949) — departure, initiation, return — overlaps with Propp and underwrites contemporary screenwriting from Star Wars to Harry Potter.
